ELI5: Why does alcohol have so many calories?
Alcohol is pretty much liquid energy, you can even burn it if it's strong enough. And energy is counted in calories.

It's basically half digested sugar, so it shouldn't be too surprising it's got most of the calories. Also, most yeast only get to about 1/2-3/4 of the sugar so the residual is there if you're not distilling it (beer and wine) and it's common to mix liquor with strong sweeteners.

So alcohol has a high energy density as other people are saying, but the reason humans can absorb these calories unlike other energy dense substances like cellulose is that way back in early human history before we had farming we had to eat whatever we found. Most of the fruit we found was already partially rotten and fermented, so we evolved to be able to digest the ethanol present in it.
Alcohol has so many calories because it's the second most calorie dense macronutrient after fat. Fat = 9 calories per gram Alcohol = 7 calories per gram Carbohydrate & Protein = 4 calories per gram

Alcohol is actually ethanol. The chemical formula for ethanol is C2H5OH... which is just a carbohydrate.

Now, you should understand what a carbohydrate is: "carbo" states that it's a main carbon chain molecule, and "hydrate" signals all of the hydrogen molecules which make up the rest of the molecule, and there's an oxygen in there... but let's ignore the oxygen, because we're trying to keep things simple...

Now, all organic energy is stored as a form of carbohydrates... glucose is a chain of carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen; gasoline is C8H18, which is also a carbon chain; propane, butane, methane (farts), and anything you can imagine we burn for heat or energy is primarily a carbon chain.

The reason these carbon chains are such great sources of energy is because the carbon-hydrogen chains can burn with oxygen and produce simpler molecules of water (H2O) and carbon dioxide (CO2). The trick is that it takes more energy to hold ethanol/glucose together than it does to hold CO2 and H2O together. When converted to water and CO2, all of this extra energy is released from every ethanol/glucose molecule in the form of heat... same goes with gasoline, which is why when you burn gasoline in the presence of oxygen, it explodes with such "energy." When you think about millions upon millions of TINY molecules releasing massive amounts of energy when they're converted down to simpler molecules, you realize that these carbohydrates are an EXCELLENT source of stored energy.

Now, since ethanol is one of these "high energy" hydrocarbons, and we can consume it, and we don't always need to "burn" it immediately... we're usually sitting down to dinner, or chatting with friends at a bar, or watching the TV in our living rooms when we're drinking this hydrocarbon we call ethanol... our body converts this alcohol into glucose, and stores it into our fat cells as a calorie, which is actually a unit of measure for energy, like a Joule.

When the time comes that we need it, we can then further convert that glucose into CO2 and utilize that stored energy we call calories.

ELI5: What is the NSA and what's the whole deal with it?

NSA Wikipedia Link

The National Security Agency (NSA) is an intelligence organization of the United States government, responsible for global monitoring, collection, and processing of information and data for foreign intelligence and counterintelligence purposes – a discipline known as signals intelligence (SIGINT). NSA is concurrently charged with protection of U.S. government communications and information systems against penetration and network warfare.[8][9] Although many of NSA's programs rely on "passive" electronic collection, the agency is authorized to accomplish its mission through active clandestine means,[10] among which are physically bugging electronic systems[11] and allegedly engaging in sabotage through subversive software.[12][13] Moreover, NSA maintains physical presence in a large number of countries across the globe, where its Special Collection Service (SCS) inserts eavesdropping devices in difficult-to-reach places. SCS collection tactics allegedly encompass "close surveillance, burglary, wiretapping, breaking and entering".[14][15]
